summary:
**KOSPI 2027 Outlook: Heavily Tied to Samsung & SK Hynix Memory Recovery**

As of late November 2026, the KOSPI sits at multi-month lows (around 4,708 after a -3.3% session), down ~48% from its June 2026 record high of 9,114. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together dominate the index (historically ~50%+ combined weight) and have led the decline, falling 51.8% and 62.9% from 52-week highs respectively.[[1]](https://x.com/VoidReader_/status/2124805812505702528)

### Analyst Consensus on 2027 Fundamentals
Despite the price collapse, **2027 earnings forecasts have been rising**, not falling:

- Combined 2027 operating profit estimates for Samsung + SK Hynix rose 21.1% from end-June levels to 1,078.3 trillion won.[[2]](https://x.com/Schulz_Research/status/2124862581554786585)
- KB Securities (Nov 2026): DRAM demand +25% vs supply +18% → ASP +40%; NAND demand +19% vs flat supply → ASP +30%.[[3]](https://x.com/J2Wick/status/2123538260534391136)
- Goldman Sachs: 2027 supply tightness remains intact due to AI compute demand; prices already bake in zero AI capex growth in 2028 and a further 40% memory price drop.[[4]](https://x.com/carrioresearch/status/2124726104246358482)
- Earlier Macquarie projections (Feb 2026 context, still referenced): Massive revenue growth into 2027, implying forward P/Es as low as 2.2–3.7x.[[5]](https://x.com/aleabitoreddit/status/2026529571990839302)

Stocks are now trading at record-low multiples that price in an earnings cliff analysts do not see:
- Samsung: ~2.58x 12-month forward P/E
- SK Hynix: ~2.14x 12-month forward P/E
- Samsung ~1.2x 2027E PBR; SK Hynix ~1.1x 2027E PBR[[2]](https://x.com/Schulz_Research/status/2124862581554786585)

JPMorgan and others view current levels as already reflecting a 70%+ earnings collapse that is not materializing, thanks to long-term contracts, customer prepayments, and tight HBM supply.[[6]](https://x.com/MelvinInvests/status/2120003533630222751)

### Market Sentiment vs Reality Gap
The sharp sell-off reflects:
- Fears of AI capex slowdown/financing issues
- US-China export restrictions
- Broader risk-off in semis

Yet Korean authorities have a stabilization fund on standby, have eased buyback limits, and are cracking down on illegal short-selling.[[1]](https://x.com/VoidReader_/status/2124805812505702528)

### 2027 Base Case
**Bullish for Samsung & SK Hynix (and thus KOSPI)** if AI-driven memory demand holds. The 2027 supply-demand imbalance remains favorable (especially HBM), with earnings momentum intact and valuations at generational lows. Goldman and others maintain Buy ratings even after recent price target cuts, citing 17–22% shareholder yields and stress-tested floors already priced in.[[4]](https://x.com/carrioresearch/status/2124726104246358482)

**Risks** remain elevated: any material slowdown in hyperscaler capex, further geopolitical shocks, or a broader recession could pressure the names. However, the market appears to have front-run a downturn that consensus forecasts have not.

**Bottom line**: KOSPI’s 2027 trajectory is essentially a bet on Samsung and SK Hynix. Current prices embed extreme pessimism that contrasts with rising earnings estimates and tight fundamentals. This setup is viewed by multiple sell-side firms as a potential “priced for disaster” opportunity rather than a fair-value reflection of 2027 reality.
